WD 4TB Blue-Black My Passport Ultra Metal Edition Portable External Hard Drive - USB 3.0 - WDBEZW0040BBA-NESN I had a big clunky WD My Book Essential 1Tb USB 3.0 external drive and it was getting old and failing.
I received this Ultra Metal 2Tb model today.
I actually took the old My Book apart by prying the case off with a large screwdriver and removed the bare HDD from inside. There is a WD Green drive in there and I actually mounted it in my computer, wiped and formatted it and now it gives me 1Tb of extra storage, not bad.
So, the Ultra Metal external drive is so classy.
The only complaint I have is the included USB 3.0 cable, it is very short, maybe 12 inches long, not good, however, I had the other 3.0 cable from the old drive, it's about 1 meter long, and it of course works fine with the new drive, I have it plugged into a 1 meter USB 3.0 extension cable so now have about 6 feet of wiggle room from the computer to the external drive.
I like this Blue- Black Ultra Metal drive's aesthetics, it is, in short, gorgeous.
That big boxy My Book I had before was so clunky, big and ran hot all the time.
This device has no unnecessary power cable, just one USB port and nothing else.
I opened the file for this drive and saw about 5Mb of preinstalled apps installers including a PDF Users Manual and quite a few other apps in about 20 different languages.
WD has gone to a lot of effort to make this drive world class.
Except for that little 12 inch USB 3.0 cable. Get yourself an extension cable and this drive is the Cadillac of external drives. The included software is icing on the cake for you to choose how sweet you will make your drive.

(72 x 108 inch) Pure White Backdrop Screen, 100% Pure Seamless Background, High Density 150 GSM Fabric with Elastic String Clips for Photo Video Streaming Studio, JSAG103 Even though I am a photographer, I didn't buy these for photography backdrops. I bought them to use as curtains for my master bedroom and, for that, they are perfect!

They are very lightweight, almost obliquely translucent at times, and they aren't stitched super well (there are little threads you'll need to clip), but otherwise, they are PERFECT. They steam VERY easily when hung (a problem with a lot of thicker backdrops), are super soft and gorgeous when hung.

The only other problem I have with them is that the last one of five I have ordered came stained in several areas--and it's stained with something grey-tan that neither washes or even bleaches out. So...it's going back.

Still, all in all, these are SUCH a find for the price! If I decide to get more to use as a photo backdrop, I'd get two and layer them, because just one will likely show whatever is behind it, and they would also easily show tension if you try to place anything like a chair or other prop on them.

text_fidelity_a:
Philips Universal Remote Control for Samsung, Vizio, LG, Sony, Sharp, Roku, Apple TV, TCL, Panasonic, Smart TVs, Streaming Players, Blu-ray, DVD, 4 Device, Walnut, SRP4320W/27 We can not find the remote for our Roku or downstairs TV which is a Samsung since we had to remodel over a long period of time due to a flood which started it all. I thought this would be perfect.

BUTTONS
The layout and buttons of this remote are pretty small. They are not difficult to use, however. The explanation in the instructions is pretty good.

USING WITH SAMSUNG AND ROKU
I have an older Samsung TV and a Roku Premiere hooked up to it. At first this worked fine with the TV, but the Roku it just would not work. Finally, I hit the SET UP button and held it until it blinked. I used the S button (next to the TV button) and suddenly instead of having to program the Roku, it just started to work. I did not have to enter roku codes at all.

DOES IT WORK WITH BOTH WELL?
Both of those things work well. I might try to set up DVD later, but for now, all I really wanted was to have the Roku and TV to work. I have a separate satellite remote that I use for DISH so I am not that interested in using this for that as it is upstairs. I would love a Sleep button like my other Samsung remote has, but really that is not a big deal for this particular TV.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For me, once I put in the two AAA batteries, this remote took almost no time to set up for my older Samsung TV and Roku Premiere.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. I wish this had a sleep setting to it, but that is minor. It does what I want it to and runs both Roku and Samsung TV nicely.
text_fidelity_b: Philips Universal Remote Control for Samsung, Vizio, LG, Sony, Sharp, Roku, Apple TV, TCL, Panasonic, Smart TVs, Streaming Players, Blu-ray, DVD, 4 Device, Walnut, SRP4320W/27

text_fidelity_a:
Echo Glow - Multicolor smart lamp, a Certified for Humans Device – Requires compatible Alexa device I am not the target demographic for this device: middle-aged empty nester who loves to watch sci-fi, thrillers, and horror. I have a number of these brilliantly simple, highly configurable lights. They are perfect in the bedroom where, depending on our intended mood, a variety of different colors or modes might be appropriate. I have two in the living room, hiding behind tropical plants at a 3' height, on either side of the big screen, about 5 feet away on each side. I have a routine set up to turn off all the lights in the room and engage campfire mode in both lights at 45% brightness with a single keyword. Voila--instant torchlight in the jungle (or romantic candlelight - take your pick). I am a colossal LOST fan, and this lighting is perfect for watching LOST, or anything scary or dark. And if I need a different effect, that's only a few words away.

The simplicity with which these set up and configure themselves is so good it makes Apple products jealous. If you have an Alexa on your Wi-Fi network, simply plug the Glow in to a power source, open the Alexa app on your phone, and the light will auto-connect to your network and add itself to Alexa. It will then prompt you to configure it with a name and add it to any groups, etc. Utterly simple. If the setup fails, it might ask you to scan the barcode on the back of the booklet it came with to get it going, but this has not been my experience - they have all self-configured and join the network seamlessly.

For those of you complaining this does not have a mic and speaker - folks, it works WITH an Echo device. It is a light - that's it. If Amazon built Alexa mics and speakers into this it would cost double--and I am positive they are developing just such a light ...for which you will pay $60+.

Normally, these are $30/ea, but they were 45% off on Prime Day, so I added a few more. There are indeed cheaper (and much more expensive) smart mood lights on the market, but if you run Alexa at home, this is hands down the best way to do it. Seamless.

It baffles me that Amazon does not have a whole range of lighting products which work exactly like this. They easily could. Give me one of these on a larger scale (12-15") and make it weatherproof for outside on the patio, please.
text_fidelity_b: Echo Glow - Multicolor smart lamp, a Certified for Humans Device – Requires compatible Alexa device

text_fidelity_a:
Portable Pocket WOWOTO Projector Android Mini Smart LED DLP Projector I was actually really shocked at how great this little portable speaker is. My cell phone found it in seconds, and in less than a minute I was listening to music from my cell phone, only out of this little speaker, it actually sounded great. In fact, the bass was so effective out of this thing that some of my favorite songs made it dance around the table.

I love that it is so much louder than the music I get out of my cell phone, and I also love that I can listen to hip-hop and rap and enjoy actual bass, which usually doesn't come through for my cell phone speaker at all.

You can actually control the music from your cell phone from the speaker itself. It has a pause/play button, forward and back, and volume controls. It also has a speakerphone control, in case you wanted to have a quick conversation from the speaker itself. I would not personally want to use the speaker as a speakerphone, but it is nice to have the option in a pinch.

The one thing I didn't care for is that when you tap the volume button and it hits its maximum, it beeps at you to let you know that it won't go any louder. It's a pretty annoying sound, and in my view they could just have left that feature out. I'm sure I would figure it out soon enough that it wouldn't go any louder.

Overall, I was really surprised at the quality, ease of setup, and range of sound from this cute little speaker. I'm delighted to own it, and anticipate it getting a lot of use over the coming months and years.
text_fidelity_b: Portable Pocket WOWOTO Projector Android Mini Smart LED DLP Projector

HUION Keydial Mini Bluetooth Programmable Keypad with Dial 5 Keys Anti-ghosting 18 Customized Keys, Wireless Shortcut Keyboard for Drawing Tablet, PC, MacBook, Surface Pro, Laptops I'm no artist in any way but I do want to try getting into digital art. As a present to myself, I purchased the [[ASIN:B083W88L5H Huion Kamvas 13]] to get started. Huion is known for providing great quality in their products while keeping the prices affordable.

As anyone who has used a drawing tablet can attest, with the tablet taking up the main desk space, it's difficult to access the keyboard for all the shortcut keys that help to make the job easier. One option is to use an under-the-desk keyboard tray, but I really don't like doing that as I tend to kick the tray when I get in and out of my chair. Others purchase more expensive hotkey devices such as this one.

While the HUION Mini KeyDial KD100 does not have fancy led lights or e-ink display on the keys, it does have the basics of what one would need. The keys are laid out like the number pad on a full 101-key keyboard and the dial can be used to adjust anything that needs a kind of analog input (volume, zoom, brush size, etc). The keys are preconfigured for the most common shortcuts but each key can be customized.

The Mini KeyDial came in an oddly plain white box with the name Huion printed on top. It's almost like this is a rebranded white-box device but that really isn't a problem. It simply means that the unboxing experience isn't as satisfying as the drawing tablet itself. Once connected to the Huion drivers, the device feels fully integrated to Huion's ecosystem.

It is managed in the same driver/software that Huion uses for its tablets so that once you'll be able to get up and running customizing the buttons immediately.

Last thing to point out is that the dial on this device can support Microsoft's own RaDial drivers to emulate the dial that Microsoft introduced a few years ago for the Surface Studio, allowing it to interact natively with built-in Windows utilities.
text_fidelity_b: HUION Keydial Mini Bluetooth Programmable Keypad with Dial 5 Keys Anti-ghosting 18 Customized Keys, Wireless Shortcut Keyboard for Drawing Tablet, PC, MacBook, Surface Pro, Laptops

text_fidelity_a:
Apple 80 GB iPod AAC/MP3 Video Player 5.5 Generation (Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I got one of these for the holidays last year (12/06) and I was totally stoked. This was my first iPod--what a shame that it turned out to be such a fragile, poorly engineered device. I mean, this thing got dropped once from about 2.5 feet (it was only 2 months old) and it was TOAST (and it was in a plastic hardshell case!). I have had Laptops that survived worse. Come to think of it, I've had a lot of (far cheaper) devices that are better able to take abuse than this $400 item--including TV remotes, cell phones, Nintendo Game Boys (designed to be nearly indestructible), OTHER MP3 PLAYERS, etc. It seems that a physically appealing design does not necessarily equate to superior engineering--quite the opposite in this case. I do like it, and the replacement I got from Apple works very well. It's great looking and it does the job well. Too bad I'm so terrified of dropping it that I had to buy a big, bulky silicone case to improve its chances of survival. Let me tell ya, in its crash-test-dummy outfit, it no longer looks even the slightest bit sleek.

Have you ever dropped your keys when getting out of the car? Your cell phone? If you answered yes to either of the above, then you can probably expect to drop your iPod one day. I hope you have a (thickly) carpeted garage--or that it lands on your foot. Bottom line: If I were thinking of getting an MP3 player, iPod or another brand, it would have zero moving parts; on other words, I would buy a flash-based device instead of one with a hard drive.

I also cannot help but wonder why Nintendo does not take what they have learned about building child-proof, nearly indestructible portable gaming devices and apply this to a worthy competitor to the iPod. I would be the first in line...

I gave this product 3 stars because it does a good job of what it is touted to do: play MP3s & video/images. In fact, the user interface, including the GUI and the click wheel is one of the nicest, most intuitive designs I have ever seen on a piece of consumer electronics equipment. Too bad it's put together so cheaply. Grossly overpriced? Most definitely. I hope the iPhone turns out to be a higher quality piece.

---

UPDATE: 8/2013: still working fine... :)
text_fidelity_b: Apple 80 GB iPod AAC/MP3 Video Player 5.5 Generation (Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Even as these products rose more and more to popularity, I scoffed and resisted.

Those days are long gone. After I borrowed them from my friend for a day and tried them myself, I knew why. After getting them, these quickly became a non-negotiable part of my life. I use them to:

- take and receive meetings
- freely go pee, refill coffee, and wash my dishes while listening to a meeting
- go on runs while listening to music
- ignore noisy people around me
- get myself into a state of focus
- calm my anxiety on airplanes
- show people I am not interested to talk to them
- as a fashion statement

Seriously, I wear these so much I think I am developing a bald spot. Maybe that's why all the engineers are bald. The sound quality is superb, and so is the bluetooth range and connectivity. I have since tried the Sony's, Dolby dimensions, the newer model of these, but these are the best one. I have bought a pair for my whole family, and replaced my old pair when it got old without a second thought. One time, I tried my friend's airpods and almost threw up at the sound quality. Not to mention, with this size, they are much harder to lose.

These are my favorite product of the last several years (this, and the divacup) and I would wholeheartedly recommend!

It makes it easy to hook to bluetooth and lets me either leave my phone behind when running or pull up a weight training app. The only drawback at all is that for the first about 2 minutes, it can have tiny skips if you are also running GPS, probably something to do with the watch not quite keeping up initially.

text_fidelity_a:
Acer Aspire C24-865-ACi5NT AIO Desktop, 23.8" Full HD, 8th Gen Intel Core i5-8250U, 12GB DDR4, 1TB HDD, 802.11ac WiFi, Wireless Keyboard and Mouse, Windows 10 Home I really like this ACER ASPIRE C24-865-ACi5NT ALL-IN-ONE DESKTOP PC. It’s my first all-in-one PC, and I love the small footprint, single power cable, and easy, easy setup. It’s a true plug-and-play machine that takes about 10 minutes to unbox, assemble, and start up.

The first boot takes a while, as Win10 Home makes itself presentable, and you need to get a big Win10 update when you first check for system updates, but it’s a terrific machine for home users who aren’t gamers. (Gamers need powerful, superfast machines with specialized graphics cards.) This PC is plenty fast for ordinary home users--it boots quickly, and loads files quickly.

KEYBOARD AND MOUSE. I don’t understand the other reviewers’ dislike of the Acer keyboard and mouse. These work off a dongle (a small radio receiver that you plug into a USB 2.0 port at the back of the monitor) when the mouse is turned on. The dongle is stored inside the mouse’s battery compartment. Both keyboard and mouse are sensitive, and I actually like the feel of the keyboard better than the feel of a very nice Verbatim quiet-key keyboard (with mouse) that I own that also works from a radio dongle.

The keyboard does have square, flat keys that aren’t at all elegant-looking. However, if you’re used to typing on an iPad’s virtual keyboard or on a laptop, you won’t mind the flat keys. The dongle eliminates two cables (one for the keyboard, one for the mouse), so you can move both mouse and keyboard off your desk if you aren’t using the PC.

DISPLAY: Not being an expert on technical display specs, all I can say is that the display has accurate color and excellent high-definition images. The size of the display (23.8”) is perfect for a PC that lives on your desk (where you’re always sitting close to it). Also, the edge-to-edge display makes this look like an expensive monitor!

OPERATING SYSTEM, CAMERA, JACKS AND PORTS: Windows 10 Home is powerful enough, and full-featured enough, for my general home use. I use this PC for checking mail, connecting to the Internet, playing a few simple games (e.g., Microsoft Solitaire), occasionally meeting with people via Skype, keeping financial records, and composing a few letters. The system comes with free online Microsoft Word, and with a 1-month free trial of Microsoft Office 365 ($99 a year if you keep it).

Wireless is built in. My PC had no difficulty connecting to my home network--connections are handled by the Win10 operating system. Stereo sound is built in, and sounds good to my non-audiophile ears.

The webcam is kind of pathetic, with very poor picture quality. However, people are recognizable, and you can easily replace the webcam with a better one. The webcam isn’t built-in, but attaches magnetically to the monitor and plugs into a USB port in back.

On the back of the monitor, the PC has an SD card reader, an audio jack (for headphones, and I think microphone too), a Kensington lock, an ethernet port, a PS2 port, a VGA port, an HDMI/DP port, and four USB ports (two 2.0 ports, with one being used by the dongle; and two 3.0 ports, with one being used by the webcam). If four USB ports aren’t enough for you, you can easily use one or more of the USB ports to add USB-port hubs.

STORAGE: The hard drive (inside the monitor) has a 1 terabyte capacity, which will store tons of photos and doc files. If you need more storage, you can add a USB storage drive.

SUMMARY: This is an extremely well-thought-out general purpose PC. It’s a space-saver, and it’s extraordinarily easy to set up. The only hard thing is understanding that the keyboard and mouse work by radio, and locating the receiver dongle inside the mouse.
text_fidelity_b: Acer Aspire C24-865-ACi5NT AIO Desktop, 23.8" Full HD, 8th Gen Intel Core i5-8250U, 12GB DDR4, 1TB HDD, 802.11ac WiFi, Wireless Keyboard and Mouse, Windows 10 Home

One of them is for power, and I've got a wireless mouse and keyboard, which leaves one port for everything else.
Needless to say, I need a few more ports and also an ethernet connection (RJ45).
The unit comes nicely boxed and for some reason has a bunch of stickers for the flags of various countries. Not sure why, but it's an interesting approach.
It has a lot of ports, an HDMI, RJ45,SD Card and micro SD, 1 USB C, 1 PD, which looks like a USB C, but is a power port, 2 USB 2.0 and 2 USB 3.0.
There is a warning label that says it might get hot (up to 130" F) and thatdevices with power higher than 7.5W are not supported, so check on the things you will be plugging into the hub before you buy it. It also says the PD adapter is under 40W and may not be able to charge all devices through the hub.
So, if you are going to use this to power a bunch of USB devices or charge your phones, it might not work. But if you are just plugging things in like cameras, microphones or drives then it will work fine.
For having all those ports, it's not as large as some others I've used and all in all is a nice hub. If you need more ports, then this is definitely worth considering.

text_fidelity_a:
Canon Powershot A1200 12.1 MP Digital Camera with 4x Optical Zoom (Silver) (OLD MODEL) OK, here are the facts: my other (similar) camera developed a glitch -- it will not allow me to delete photos without loooooong delays. So I went in search of an inexpensive replacement camera. I settled on this Canon.

I did so with trepidation because some of the reviews were lukewarm at best. Yet other reviewers loved it. (This, by the way, is what makes horse races!) So I thought I would take a chance.

Here is why I am happy with my choice: (1) the viewer seems larger than its dimensions suggest; (2) the camera fits in my shirt pocket; (3) the pics are crisp indoors and out; (4) the on-off button is clearly marked and the shot button is nice and robust. For me, these features are all I need. To be sure, the camera has a few video bells and whistles -- I'll try those one of these days. No rush.

A Con: the shot button takes a little getting used to, since it appears to have two stages to it. If you just press and disengage, nothing will happen. It requires a little patience and then it will take the picture. I can live with that idiosyncrasy.

Another Con: no internal memory. You must purchase an SD card before you can use the camera. This too I have accepted, because having pics on cards does make it easy to load them into PCs and laptops.

If you are looking for a simple "point-and-shoot" camera that will also perform other tricks if you are of a mind, go for it!
text_fidelity_b: Canon Powershot A1200 12.1 MP Digital Camera with 4x Optical Zoom (Silver) (OLD MODEL)

The battery compartment is easy to access, no hassle replacing the single battery. I comes with a brand name battery uninstalled which is very nice. However, it's too lightweight for my tastes. The “click” feels cheap to me and the scroll wheel is stiff. I won't send this Microsoft mouse back, but I wouldn't buy it again. I haven't had any problems with this mouse, it's just personal preference. I'll just use the Microsoft as a travel mouse. Bose SoundLink On-Ear Bluetooth Wireless Headphones - Black All I can politely write is that what an amazing experience. The headphones are small and just sit over the ears (like their noise canceling headphones). The Bluetooth component sits neatly inside the headphones, as we have another Bose Bluetooth headphones and the Bluetooth component sits outside of the headphones. I synced this with iPad, iPhone and iPod Classic (using Kokkia I10). The quality of the sound is fabulous as you would expect from BOSE ( a lot of bass) you will not be disappointed. I played a range of music from rock, pop and classical music...awesomeness is the experience with Bose! The range is not miles...more like 20 feet..and not through too many walls. ...terrific design of compactness and total comfort on my ears. In terms of external noise, it really did cut out the concrete jungle living of traffic hum.

I listened to my music for over an hour now and no pain on my ears...bliss and worth every cent and pennies. I love these new BOSE Bluetooth headphones. Note, they come fully charged. There are little and discreet volume up and down buttons, which are elevated a little so it is easy to find and you will not end up pushing the wrong button. I didn't have to press any additional button to synch..there is a voice telling you that it is seeking to synch..and will let you know when it has connected. There is a button to switch from music to speak on the phone. Crystal clear. It comes with a power charge..a micro USB cable and a RCA cable.(hmm redundant with Bluetooth, but if you have digital piano, you can connect it via the RCA. I am going to get the Bluetooth adaptor to test it with these head phones).

The headphones remember all the names of the gadgets, and will play from which ever one that is 'on', which is a huge plus. There appears to be an intelligence here that we do not see in the Bose over the ear wireless headphones.

In term of play time, after a full charge, which took less than 2 hours: total playtime is more like 8 hours, not 15 hours claimed, but it must be related to the volume too. I had my volume pretty high most of the time. Given, how quickly it charged up, and the number of hours of playtime, I really don't need to charge it up for more than one every three days.

I have tried several other similar devices and they all had serious problems, while this provides 87W of power, dual display support (DisplayPort 1.2), both an analogue and digital audio (TOSLINK) device, SD card reader, and extra 5 Gbps Thunderbolt 3/USB-C and USB 3.0 ports.

Regarding the 1 star reviews, with the exception of the person with the defective unit, I am almost positive the problems people have been having are because of their cables. To connect your computer to the dock, use the cable they provide. If you need a longer cable, be sure to buy an actual Thunderbolt 3 cable that is less than 2 meters long. As for your display cables, it is critical the cable is DisplayPort 1.2. I also connected the second monitor to the Thunderbolt 3 port that converted to DisplayPort 1.2 (I just got the Amazon Basics brand and it works as it should. I have used this on both my 2017 and 2019 MacBooks and they both work flawlessly. Its so nice to just have one cable to plug and unplug for all devices!

ANNKE C800 4K 8MP PoE Security Camera with Audio Recording, 4K Ultra HD IP Turret Camera, 100ft EXIR 2.0 Night Vision, H.265+, IP67 Weatherproof, Support 256GB SD Card(Not Included) When I initially saw this camera it checked most of the boxes I look for when looking for security cameras. It is PoE, has H.265, ONVIF support allowing use with Blue Iris, Sony IMX274 Starvis Sensor. Once I received this camera and began digging into it I quickly realized certain important facts.

Most importantly, this is a rebranded Hikvision camera. This is among the companies that has been discovered spying on the US using their cameras - the firmware this camera comes with is long outdated and, in fact, can not be updated to anywhere close to what is current. This is far too risky for me to install on my system.

Any camera you install on your system should have the latest firmware installed and you need to have a good understanding of network security protocols. Cameras such as this one, that are older versions of cameras made by manufacturers that are blacklisted - while still being sold, people who understand the industry avoid them - are an invitation for hackers to invade your system.

While the specs on and price of this camera seem decent - this is not a camera I recommend. This poses far more risks than it is worth.
text_fidelity_b: ANNKE C800 4K 8MP PoE Security Camera with Audio Recording, 4K Ultra HD IP Turret Camera, 100ft EXIR 2.0 Night Vision, H.265+, IP67 Weatherproof, Support 256GB SD Card(Not Included)

text_fidelity_a:
Lexar E-Series 128GB Micro SD Card 2 Pack, microSDXC UHS-I Flash Memory Card with Adapter, 100MB/s, C10, U3, A1, V30, Full HD, 4K UHD, High Speed TF Card I've owned a few Lexar USB drives and Micro USB drives in the past and they have all had good quality and performance. I've attached the crystal diskmark performance below, but keep in mind that I am using the built-in microsd reader in my computer so speeds may vary as the reader has just as much to do with these benchmarks as the memory card itself.

I don't have any equipment that really stresses the microsd too much. The cameras that I have, while they can record up to 4K at 30fps, have generally had no problem writing to a U1 microsd. The Lexar, which I keep in my Osmo Pocket, is no exception, it has not had an issue recording video.

There is one key thing to point out about Lexar storage media that I've experienced in two of my past devices and that is the built-in expiration or time-bomb (if you don't agree with this philosophy). Lexar seems to have the philosophy that keeping your data intact is the most important when it comes to these products. Solid-state storage media has a theoretical limit to how many times they can be written to. Once that is hit, the media will be permanently damaged. Lexar has written into their firmware, a hard limit that once you write a certain number of times to their media, it will become read-only, keeping your data intact, but the storage unusable from that point on.

While I've experienced failed media in the past, I really only had this behavior with Lexar. I have to say, it did save my wife from losing the pictures on her phone if the card failed instead of becoming read-only.
text_fidelity_b: Lexar E-Series 128GB Micro SD Card 2 Pack, microSDXC UHS-I Flash Memory Card with Adapter, 100MB/s, C10, U3, A1, V30, Full HD, 4K UHD, High Speed TF Card

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech MX Vertical Wireless Mouse – Advanced Ergonomic Design Reduces Muscle Strain, Control and Move Content Between 3 Windows and Apple Computers (Bluetooth or USB), Rechargeable, Graphite I haven't had this for very long yet, so I can't comment on longevity, but so far I like it. I take it for granted that there will be some sacrifices when using this type of mouse, I just don't expect to get the same flexibility and usability in terms of various buttons and their placements, so I can't really knock it for being a bit worse in that area than some regular, non-ergonomic options. It works very well and the buttons are easy to click and have a nice "click" to them (unlike cheaper ones). Of course, it takes some time to get used to an upright mouse if you haven't used one before, but after a while it becomes easy/natural.

Regarding the wrist angle, I had some wrist pain and in the past I'd used a cheaper upright ergonomic mouse to help. This is not carpal tunnel, I get joint inflammation on the top side of my wrist, so it may be a bit unusual.
When my old ergonomic mouse broke I decided to try a more expensive one in hopes it will last longer. I can't provide any definitive conclusions on whether this particular aspect of my "treatment" really does anything. My ultimate conclusion is that while treating with other things (e.g. braces, compression, cold or hot), using an alternate device sometimes to change the stress points probably doesn't hurt. Sometimes when going back to use my normal mouse, just putting my hand into position seems to cause some strain, so I think this upright position is helping some. But my experience is that if I use anything for too long, I'll find some joint and/or muscle getting stressed. I'm concerned that this upright mouse position may not be as good for my elbow. So my conclusion is mix it up to spread out the strain rather than hammering on a single weak area, and try to be more careful in the future to start treatment sooner, when I see the early warning signs of strain, before it gets bad.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech MX Vertical Wireless Mouse – Advanced Ergonomic Design Reduces Muscle Strain, Control and Move Content Between 3 Windows and Apple Computers (Bluetooth or USB), Rechargeable, Graphite

text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Basics On-Ear Headphones I use headphones very frequently under a number of different environments including noisy computer labs, airplanes, quiet rooms and more. I am particularly familiar with noise canceling phones but I do have a some non-ANC phones that I use for listening to music in quiet environments. This pair of Amazon Basics headphones is my least expensive pair but it actually compares reasonably well against some more expensive phones.

First, the Basics headphones are very lightweight on-ear phones. They are slightly tight though not so tight to cause discomfort. What they do cause for me is a bit of warmth on the ears, something that I have not experienced very often when using headphones. It’s a minor aggravation, not a show-stopper by any means.

The most important feature of any headphones is the sound profile. I like electronic music which has a wide range of sound frequency - abundant highs, full midrange and quite a bit of bass. When listening to tracks with these phones, the first thing that I could not help but notice is that they overdrive the bass a little much, but this seems to be more the norm with headphones anymore. The highs sound just about right - not exceptionally sharp but not muted either. The midrange, though, is off and reminds me of listening to music in a tunnel. It isn’t terrible, but it’s noticeable. From what I can tell, the bass is so overdriven that it partially flattens the midrange.

I compared these headphones to a pair of Munitio PRO40 phones, a much more expensive set ($350 full retail) of phones that I use for studio work. Yes, the Munitio phones outperformed the Basics phones, but the difference did not match the $300 price difference. Other than the midrange, the Basics phones compared very well on the sound spectrum. That’s more than I could have asked for at $15.

If this was an expensive set of phones I would be very upset. However, this is a VERY inexpensive set and for the price range sounds much better than average.

Construction-wise this set of phones feels well-made. They won’t hold up to abuse, but with proper care they should last a long time. They even come with a cloth carry bag with offers little more than scratch protection but it’s a nice touch.

Considering how inexpensive these headphones are, I am hard-pressed to criticize. In their price range they are well above average in terms of sound and construction. If you are looking for a lightweight and inexpensive set of headphones and you do not need the very best in sound this is an outstanding value.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics On-Ear Headphones

For it's size it rocked out in my back porch. Due to the IP64 rating it's a bit heavy but that's a good thing.

I tested this speaker paired with a Sony android phone. Bluetooth pairing was instant. While I didn't quite get a full 30 foot range, I found the actual 27 foot range to be acceptable.

I dropped the speaker from my waist height of 36" onto the concrete pad on my porch. No issues with playability or broken pieces. Although I did notice a slight scuff mark. No biggie.

I like the carabiner feature for hanging the speaker, from a tent ceiling, tree, or post. But I don't see anyone hanging the speaker off a backpack. The weight will cause it to swing wildly. In fact it's heavy enough to be stored in the bottom of your pack.

Recharging was easy, but the rubber plug takes a little finesse to put it back into place.

The sound was crisp with somewhat deep bass undertones. I didn't expect this little speaker to pump out heavy bass, but it's adequate for its size.

I don't recommend that you crank this up too loud when camping in the woods. The loud music might drown out the sounds of an attacking bear or wildebeest.

For the money it's a decent wireless speaker that will survive most outdoor adventures.

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech USB Headset Stereo H650e This is a decent, serviceable headset but rather expensive for the price. I have another Logitech headset for home use but this one was definitely better in quality.

Appearance: the plastic casing feels a little cheap, which raises questions about its durability. I once owned a Sharper Image headphone that had a similar feel, and it broke after a year or so.

Function: the headphone is lightweight and quite comfortable to wear, thanks to the padding on the top and the ear muffs. However, the muffs are thinner than I expected. For the price, I would have liked them to be thicker and offer better noise cancellation capabilities. The microphone, however, feels professional grade, being bendable and sensitive. In addition, the long cord is very work-friendly - it's thicker than conventional cords (preventing easy tangling) and long enough for me to reach over my desk without concern that it'll tug or pop out. Also convenient are the location of the controls for volume, phone and speaker - they're on a rectangular box located on the cord itself. Cool.

However, setting up the headphone took some work. With my other Logitech headphone, all I had to do was plug it into the USB drive, let the computer recognize the device, and off I went. Here, I had to be patient and follow the specific setting instructions for Windows 8. Listening to videos and audio files worked fine, but the microphone function didn't work when my phone rang and I tried ti answer using the mike. I pressed the button but nothing happened. As it turns out, the phone function appears to work only when you're hooked up to Linc, an application that nobody in my office uses. The instructions didn't make this clear.

The sound quality is decent for business purposes but for hi-fidelity sound, it's average. I had assumed it was a noise cancelling headphone because of the padding, but I was wrong - I had no trouble hearing some of my coworkers bickering a few feet away while I was listening to a webinar. I had to up the volume to block them out.

The headphones come with a smooth zippered vinyl pouch for storage or for traveling. This was a very nice touch.

Overall this is a decent enough headphone for work but I would have given it five stars had the price been lower.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech USB Headset Stereo H650e

text_fidelity_a:
myCharge PowerGear Sound Protective Portable Charging Case for Wireless Earbuds Headphones | Custom Tray Compatible with Powerbeats & Removable for Other Brands | 1400 mAh / 1A Output The MyCharge is a handy if not tiny clamshell charging case for PowerBeat headphones, though it will work for others as well.

Pros:
The case itself has an hard outer shell that feels durable and thick. I have no fears the earbuds will be well protected inside. It opens and closes easily and tightly. As much as a case can be, it’s aesthetically pleasing—a dark, slick black with a black ribbon with red stitching running down the middle (the red stitching matches the red inside). The ribbon/band does more than add a bit of style and color; it also gives it a bit more texture so it grips the surface it’s atop better.

The plastic tray inside is designed for the PoweBeats line, so the earbuds nestle snugly (but with no need to wrestle or force them in) into an indentation so they lie flat and with a mid-section to insert the connecting wires/controls into. It’s a good fit, well-designed, and I don’t feel like I’m overstressing the wires, though I wouldn’t want to leave them in that position for a long amount of time (though I tend to worry about that sort of thin more than others)

It comes with a cable. You can use any one, but you’ll want it to be very short

The port to charge the case (the battery inside the case for sticklers) is easily accessible.

An LED on the front lets you know if the case battery is getting low

Cons
I wish the port cover felt a little more durable

Mixed or Up in the Air
I haven’t had it long enough yet to check how many charges, but I’ve gotten a few without a noticeable impact on the case battery. I don’t know if their promise of a dozen-plus will bear out, but I don’t think it’ll be far off if not.

The case isn’t really tiny (You can see the dimensions above). If you’re looking for something to slip into a pocket, then this will be a con, though it will easily fit a coat pocket. It will fit cargo pockets but you’ll definitely know it’s there. On the other hand, it doesn’t take up a lot of space, it’s quite protective, and if you’re worried about losing your expensive but very small and easy to lose earbuds, putting them in a noticeable, protective case that will also charge them back up is far from the worst idea. Personally, I’m OK with the size.

As noted, the case is designed for PowerBeats, so your mileage will vary on how well it fits some other type. My other earbuds all fits in the case without an issue, just not as snugly or neatly. That isn’t a real priority for me even ignoring the fact that I have PowerBeats.

Overall, a good value for what it does I’d say.
text_fidelity_b: myCharge PowerGear Sound Protective Portable Charging Case for Wireless Earbuds Headphones | Custom Tray Compatible with Powerbeats & Removable for Other Brands | 1400 mAh / 1A Output

text_fidelity_a:
Aluminum Laptop Stand, tomtoc Foldable Notebook Stand with Adjustable Eye-Level Ergonomic Design, Portable Laptop Holder for MacBook Air Pro, Dell XPS, Surface Laptop and More 11 to 15.6 Inch Laptop I know, you are probably thinking- what kind of idiot would try this on their LAP? I can not tell you who, but let's just say I am a witness.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This little stand folds perfectly flat. It comes in a drawstring bag which keeps it from attacking you. You see, this is VERY easy to pinch your fingers in. I have the bruises to prove it. However, once I figured it out, I was able to avoid it any more. Keeping this in the case is a GOOD thing.

HOW TO USE THIS
When I first got this, I was explaining to a certain someone that this was to keep the laptop cooler and hold it at a better angle. It was not until that certain someone was carrying on about what a stupid device it was that I realized that this someone was trying to use it on their lap. Don't do that. You won't like it.

HOW DOES IT PERFORM?
There are silicone pads and 3 settings for this stand. The pads hold the laptop in place and the stand in each setting. It holds a lightweight laptop well and the angles are good. I found using it on the right table top helps. It seems to stay put well, but if you have a really slick top, you can always put a non-skid pad under the whole thing.

THE BOTTOM LINE
As long as you are careful and only use this on the table top and are careful about not pinching your fingers, this is a nice little stand. It holds pretty well and is at a decent angle so far for our lightweight laptop.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS. It is hard to use unless you really pay attention because it can suddenly fold down pinching the fingers, so I took a star off for that. It is a nice stand so far, but I will update as we try other laptops on it over time if necessary to let you know if something changes.

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Versa Smart Watch, Peach/Rose Gold Aluminium, One Size (S & L Bands Included), Heart Rate Monitor This little device does a lot.
While it is sort of a smart watch, it sort of isn't, too. But what it does, it does well.

The good:
- Excellent selection of watch faces, including cute, clever, big, pretty, etc. You can change your face every day to match your clothes if you want.
- If I understand correctly, you can use it with other services, like Spark People.
- measures pulse, steps, miles. Tracks exercise on demand.
- motivates in numerous ways. Reminders to stand up, encouragement to finish your goal steps for the hour, challenges, even "travel" challenges that are longer term.
- large userbase. You can network with more of your friends on Fitbit than on any other fitness watch.
- big face without losing attractiveness
- large variety of replacement bands available from third parties, some very pretty.
- Can be used with many other fitness applications.
- Detects sleep surprisingly accurately
- Lots of settings options
- A decent number of apps available
- Handles the shower well
- If you never have to take it off except to charge, it's harder to lose it.
- Charges very quickly
- The charger is an awesome design and easy to use
- You can always have your alarms with you so you never miss them.

The irritating
- All changes have to be made through the app.
- If you don't sync often enough, it loses your data
- Sync can take a long time.
- The battery life is considerably shorter than I expected. It's about 2 1/2 days if I have constant sync turned off.
- Don't even bother with constant sync unless you're willing to take it off to charge a lot.
- All the music apps are paid

All in all, though, the pros are big and the cons are small. Enough that it still warrants a 5 star review.

text_fidelity_a:
VIZIO E700i-B3 70-Inch 1080p Smart LED HDTV I bought this television (I double checked the exact model number to be positive that t I am reviewing the correct one) used at an estate sale in January and it's been used daily in our master bedroom every since. The color and clarity of the picture is simply wonderful. In comparison to our brand new Sceptre 55" 1080p tv in the living room and the 3 year old Samsung in the guest room, this Vizio has the prettiest picture and best refresh rate. The Samsung has the best native sound though without a sound bar enhancement.

This Vizio is our only Smart Television and I have a Firestick on the living room tv. As of today, June 16, 2016, the Amazon app and others are all working just fine through the television's remote control with the direct access buttons. Connecting this tv to our wifi network did take several attempts and I had to update the firmware twice before it would connect and hold the connection for more than 48 hours. (To be honest, I have no idea if the former owner every actually used the internet connection so it may not have been updated before I got it) Since January, I have had no trouble with the connection or streaming. We do have a super fast internet service and a dual band router with this tv as the only thing typically streaming on one band.

My one star deduction is the tiny receiver area for the remote control. It is solidly built and has a lot of useful features, but it also has some shortcomings that prevent me from giving it 5 stars. Here are my most important plusses and minuses:

Plusses:
+ precise construction
+ important components are sturdy metal, especially the ball head and the locking mechanisms that control the center post and the legs
+ folds up compactly for easy travel
+ relatively lightweight compared to solid metal tripods
+ cold shoe is very useful for attaching a microphone or video light

Minuses:
- legs only fold out in one flat position, so this tripod can really only be used on flat level surfaces (like tabletops).
- center post cannot be pushed all the way down below the legs like with most tripods for maximum stability
- selfie-stick mode is only 12 inches long maximum
- $80 price is expensive for a tabletop-only mini-tripod

text_fidelity_a:
AKAMATE Active Noise Cancelling Headphones, Wireless Neckband Headset Bluetooth V4.2 in-Ear Waterproof Earbuds Magnetic Hi-Fi Stereo Sports Earphones with Mic, Carrying Bag There is always a run on headphones in our house. Not only are they being lost or dying, but everyone is on a constant quest for the best design and sound they can find in a bluetooth headphone. Let's see how these measure up.

WHAT ARE THESE HEADPHONES LIKE?
These headphones have a long sturdy neck band which means they will fit a variety of neck sizes. Each ear piece has a magnet on it so that when you are not using them, they will close in front of you so you won't lose them. The controls are at the end of the neck band on the right side.

ON/OFF BUTTON
Play, pause, on/off, pair can be done with this button.

VOLUME
The minus and plus of volume control is also used for skipping songs- + skip forward, - skip backward.

ANC
There is an ANC button on the right side directly behind the negative volume button which makes it easy to press them both at the same time. It does do noise canceling, but it is frustrating because it is easy to press the ANC button by mistake when also pressing the middle button.

CHARGING PORT
Charging port is on the edge of the control button area.

AI INDICATOR VOICE
The automatic voice is very dysfunctional. It only says part of words, and seems to be a bit mean sounding which makes my daughter say it feels creepy.

NOISE CANCELING
The noise canceling works beautifully on these headphones.

SOUND QUALITY
The sound quality is awesome. Highs and mids are where they should be. Bass is very good. It is not overdone but it is in balance and does not distract from the music. There are not any breakups in sound unless you walk away from the device.

BLUETOOTH RANGE
The bluetooth range seems to be good up to about 35 feet or so.

PHONE CALL QUALITY
The calls go through very well and people can hear just fine on phone calls.

BATTERY PERCENTAGE
There is no physical light indicator to tell you how much battery power you have left.

THE BOTTOM LINE
If you want a good solid set of headphones to use with phone and music that work well, are in balance, and great for listening. The controls are not as convenient as they could be, which can be frustrating at times.

MY RATING
Four stars. If the control area was set up just a little more conveniently so that you can not accidentally press the wrong buttons all of the time, they would probably be five stars.
text_fidelity_b: AKAMATE Active Noise Cancelling Headphones, Wireless Neckband Headset Bluetooth V4.2 in-Ear Waterproof Earbuds Magnetic Hi-Fi Stereo Sports Earphones with Mic, Carrying Bag

text_fidelity_a:
Acer Aspire R 15 2-in-1 Laptop, 15.6" Full HD Touch, 7th Gen Intel Core i7, GeForce 940MX, 12GB DDR4, 256GB SSD, R5-571TG-7229 (WARNING- This is an in depth review of this laptop. My goal is to help those who are truly interested in making informed buying decisions. This is done from an experiential point of view of most consumers and not highly technical. If you prefer a shorter summary, see paragraph titled, THE BOTTOM LINE)

WHAT IS THIS LAPTOP LIKE?
I have had a lot of different tablets, laptops, desktops, and have built my own systems over the years. One thing I have not had is a hybrid laptop which changes from tablet to laptop and back again. I was not too fond of a 15 inch size as I tend to like smaller laptops, but I was willing to try. I am SO glad I did.

COVERING/CASE OF LAPTOP
This laptop is a thin profile, but feels very substantial. The bottom does not have tiny little rubber feet like some HP professional laptops I have had, but it has solid large rubberized pads that are 1 inch by a half inch. There are a decent amount of vents in the bottom as well. The top is a slightly textured metallic top (etched look) and not shiny. The hinges are very strong and hold the screen in a variety of directions solidly. They do not budge until I move them again.

SIZE
I am amazed that this is the first 15 inch laptop that I actually enjoy using! The size and way that it works makes it fantastic for me. I can tilt the screen in any direction and use my hands on the screen or keyboard in laptop mode which is a pleasure.

KEYBOARD
The keyboard is soft touch and rubberized key-wise. As soon as I touch the keys, a back light comes up so that I can see what I am doing. The back light goes out in 15 seconds or so when the keys are not being pressed. There is a full numerical keyboard and plenty of room between keys for my medium sized fingertips. It is also spaced well for those who have longer nails.

SCREEN
The screen is shiny. It doubles as a screen as well as touchscreen. The view on the screen is fabulous as it has a full HD 1080 resolution. The colors are not as intense as the Saumsung Galaxy Tab S2, which is one of the most amazing color screens I have worked with. Since I am a person who likes color, I like color intensity in my screens. However, this screen is fine and is by no means pale, it is just not quite as intense as I am used to.

TOUCHSCREEN
When you flip the keyboard back, the touchscreen clicks into place. You are given the option to choose the touchscreen if you want so there are no mistakes. As a tablet, I have found that it is very accurate and works quite well. I have put it through a lot and so far, I have only had a few instances where I was frustrated for a second, but it was easy to correct.

OPERATION
This turns on so fast it is almost jolting. My laptops, though usually professional level, often take quite a bit to boot up. This one, however is so quick it always surprises everyone here.

As for operations, I have found this to be a very fast and easy to use system. Load up is quick and the only problems I have from time to time are due to wireless and not really the fault of the laptop.

Turning it off sometimes makes me laugh out loud. Press button. BAM! It’s off.

WINDOWS 10
I am not a fan of Windows 10. But unfortunately that is pretty much the choice for any laptop at this point. This laptop seems to handle it very well.

GAMES
Because Windows 10 is not as game friendly as previous operating systems, I have not had the time to mess around with games with this. I have avoided Windows 10 until now, so I have not figured out what if any games will work with this. I will update when I do.

RUN TIME
Charging seems to take only a few hours for a full charge. The run time varies between 3 and 5 hours depending on what I am doing. I will say this- I rarely run it into the ground in one sitting, which makes it very helpful for me.

VIDEO
Runs very smooth on here. Using a DVD player means I have to use the USB port to run my independent unit and be in a stable position to do so. Works well. Beautiful to watch.

USB PORTS AND SD READER
I have found the USB ports to work very well. No problems to this point. Load up is fast. Using the SD reader is also a pleasure. The photos load up fast and due to the high resolution screen viewing them is really detailed and helpful. I have not installed professional graphics software yet to test this system for photo editing.

TOUCH PAD (AND FRUSTRATION)
The touch pad on this laptop is a bit challenging to use. There is a finger reader which I do not use, but the buttons are hidden in the pad itself and not two different buttons. The pad is pretty accurate as far as tracking. The only problem I have is location. When I rest my left hand on the rest area, sometimes it interferes with the touch pad and causes things to go a bit crazy at times. I am not pressing ON the touch pad, just in the area next to it.

SOUND
The sound is not tinny or awful. I find that it is sufficient for most of the applications I want to use it for. If I prefer to have a better sound, I use my Soundbot speaker and that gives me even better sound for movies and videos.

COMMENTS
I have to say that although the touch pad situation does frustrate me now and then, I do love this laptop. I have always wanted a hybrid because since I started using tablets, I would always catch myself touching the screen when I was using one of the household laptops and it was frustrating.

This unit is really nice. It is so fast and easy to use, it surprises me, honestly. It is so easy to switch between tablet and laptop modes and I find it a pleasure to work with for photos and movies.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This hybrid is VERY fast, easy to use, and boots up and shuts down so fast it is startling. The screen is a pleasure to look at, although not as color saturated as Samsung can be. So far, USB and SD works great. Sound is good enough for most applications. This is easy to use and not at all cumbersome. I love that I can touch the screen even in laptop mode if I am frustrated with the touch pad. I am very happy with this laptop/tablet hybrid.

RATING
FIVE STARS! I will update if I have anything else to add in the future, but at this point, I am very happy with this.
text_fidelity_b: Acer Aspire R 15 2-in-1 Laptop, 15.6" Full HD Touch, 7th Gen Intel Core i7, GeForce 940MX, 12GB DDR4, 256GB SSD, R5-571TG-7229

text_fidelity_a:
Upgrade/RGB Video Light, 360 ° Full Color LED Camera Light, Dimmable 2500K-8500K Portable Pocket Size Camera Lighting, 12 Lighting Effect Mode, Built-in 3200mAh Rechargeable Battery We do jewelry photos which are very difficult to shoot, especially when iridescence is involved. We have big lights to set up and get good shots, but then we have been having issues with some of the light leaving things looking a bit dead. Enter this light. Let's take a look.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This a light that is about the size of a smart phone- well the slightly larger ones. It comes with a case that has an elastic band on one side and a net bag with elastic top on the opposite side. The kit comes with a square slide to put on the camera along with screws to hold the discs in place to stop wobble. There is a charge outlet,, a charge cord (USB on the other end) and an output cord which goes from C to USB.

HOW DOES THIS WORK?
When you turn this on, you press the power button and hold it down. The light goes on. There is a little window with the information in it.

TIME LEFT FOR USE
This tells you how many hours are left before you need to recharge so you can plan your sessions.

BATTERY
There is a battery indicator

BRIGHTNESS
From 5% to 100%

TEMPERATURE
Coolest temp being 5600K down to 3200K which is like candlelight.

DIAL
The dial on the side allows you to go up or down

POWER BUTTON DUAL MENU BUTTON
You use the power button to turn on the light, but once it is on, then if you touch it once quickly, it changes from brightness to temperature so you can set what you like. An arrow is very obvious so you know where it is set.

HOW TO ATTACH TO CAMERA
I have a Canon Poweshot G12 and this attaches up where a flash usually goes. You can screw this into the lamp either horizontally or vertically. You slide in the metal plate with the screw on it, then you screw the light onto that and use the discs to tighten up the light so it does not move.

HOW DOES THIS PERFORM?
I have to say, this little thing is amazing. It has fantastic light, works very well and even though you can use it by itself for video or interviews, etc, for jewelry photos, we need to have additional light to use with this to avoid shadows.

I have gotten some excellent photos which are really nice and with a little adjustments in photo editing turn out to be great in capturing texture, color, and iridescence.

CHARGING
I found that a few hours of charging gave me a complete charge. After using this for about three hours (I turned it off in between set ups) I still have four out of five bars on the battery indicator and about 4 hours left of predicted use time.

WILL I NEED ANOTHER LIGHT?
If you are doing product photos like we are of jewelry or something that is detailed and needs to have very good lighting, then you will probably need another light. I would say a second one of these would be perfect- set it up on a little tripod and it will be great. If you are just doing portraits, or interviews, you might be able to get away with just this light. Shadows at that point don't matter as much- unless they are severe, of course.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is one of the best things I have ever gotten for taking photos. It has really helped me take photos beautifully an I am thrilled with it. The temperature control is beautiful and the brightness controls are also excellent in increments.

MY RATING
FIVE VERY ENTHUSIASTIC STARS. This is a great portable light that goes with you anywhere. The case is great, and the light is the perfect size to toss into my camera bag when traveling.

PHOTOS
When I get some photos that I am not using on my site, I will try to post some for you. It is worth seeing.
text_fidelity_b: Upgrade/RGB Video Light, 360 ° Full Color LED Camera Light, Dimmable 2500K-8500K Portable Pocket Size Camera Lighting, 12 Lighting Effect Mode, Built-in 3200mAh Rechargeable Battery

text_fidelity_a:
Belkin N150 Wireless USB Adapter with up to 150Mbps Link Rate We have several networked devices in our house and also several individualized networks configured. Not all of the networks can be seen by all devices so I looked to this Belkin USB WiFi adapter to allow one of the older computer systems to access the most reliable network in the house - a 5GHz network that only one or two of the systems can see.

Installation was a snap. I popped in the CD, told it to install the drivers and we were off to the races. The particular target system was a 32-bit Windows Vista laptop. After just a couple of minutes the driver was completely installed and when I plugged in the USB adapter is was picked up immediately. I could see the desired network as well as several other networks in the neighborhood that were previously invisible to the computer. I shut off the built-in adapter, connected to the 5GHz network and went to the net.

So far, the connection has been very stable and speeds have been excellent. The router to which it is connected is a TP-Link router and so far we have seen no issues between the two devices. I have not had this adapter very long so it is still early to say it’s completely stable but all indicators up to this point have been very favorable.

Several other reviewers have mentioned that this adapter does not work with Linux. This is true - there are no drivers available for this adapter other than for Windows XP/Vista/7/8. If you need an adapter that will allow you to connect a Linux or Mac system to a wireless network, this is not the device you need right now.

So far I can’t find too much about which to complain concerning this router. It seems to be stable and reliable on the system to which it is attached here. I am satisfied with it and based on my experience with it can recommend it - if you’re sticking with Windows.

text_fidelity_a:
Roku Premiere - HD and 4K UHD Streaming Media Player The Roku Premiere player is easy to set up and has a well-designed user interface that requires no reference to a user manual. I connected it to the tv (using an HDMI cable), plugged it in, turned on the tv and selected the appropriate source. I was disappointed that there was no option to plug in a network cable for a wired connection (like there is for the Fire TV box; you have to go up to the Premiere+ to get that port). This might be a concern for anyone with a weak or problematic wifi signal.

The initialization was fairly simple: language selection, wifi connection (it supports AC as well as N), automatic detection of the tv display type, automatic software update, then a separate session on the computer to register the device and create a Roku account. I had another disappointment here: the account creation requires the entry of payment info, either credit card or Paypal. If I want to use the box just to watch my subscribed services, such as Netflix and Amazon, there's no reason for me to give Roku any payment information at all, it just increases the risk of malicious use. (If you really don't like this, you can sign up using a Paypal account, then go back into your Paypal account and rescind the Roku permissions.)

After that it was all plain sailing, and I had no complaints: streaming video was clear and glitch-free, the sound was good. All in all, a very nice streaming box for a reasonable price. For my money, however, I would consider upgrading to the Premiere+. Or, the Fire TV box, which is what I normally use at home.
text_fidelity_b: Roku Premiere - HD and 4K UHD Streaming Media Player

text_fidelity_a: Amazon Fire HD 8 tablet, 8” HD Display, 32 GB, 30% faster processor, designed for portable entertainment, (2022 release), Rose I have NEVER hated an electronic device more than this one.  I don't know why it doesn't show that I purchased this in 2022 (and also in 2010 - before Version 1 died).  I hate it, I really hate it.  I detest Alexa  and all the things she doesn't do but get in the way of letting you do what you want.  I hate her.  I LOVED my previous FIRE the ads were just a few seconds long and I could live with that.  But to play my favorite Spider Solitaire game I've had ads go on as long as 10 minutes,  I've had it forget to navigate back to the game and I end up having to go home and locate the correct version of Spider I was playing.  EVERYTIME I open the thing It is pure HELL trying to get to what I want.  For example, today all I kept getting was movies.  I'd go back to home, and it would still show me movies, I turned it off and back on - more movies.  When I did a search for either the book I'm currently reading (Spare) of course OR my favorite Spider Solitaire, Alexa kept displaying some kids Blue's Clues music that didn't have any of my search words in its name. After a number of tries Alexa finally found my game.  If I pay the extra to get rid of ads will that include all the ads every 10 seconds on any game, you play so you can get your points and move on with the game?  All I do is play this ONE game and read books and now I go through hell to be allowed to do it - between Alexa and Ads the device is barely usable.  Oh and get this - I was eating in the dining room (I live in Senior Independent living but I'm VERY competent on computers}  I was in the dining room reading Spare when suddenly Alexa decided she should show me how it sounded with audio and Harry started reading it to me at full volume until I figured out how to turn the volume off. It startled me and a number of others in the room - I was seriously pissed off.  I could do this on my computer, but I always use my kindle when I'm doing 4 different breathing treatments that takes over an hour or when I just want to curl up in a chair and read or every time, I get hospitalized due to lung issues.  How can I get rid of both Alexa and the ads?  I'll pay whatever it takes.  I really only have a few years left to live assuming I don't get a bad case of COVID or Influenza  (I have a weak immune system) and I don't want to waste it on Alexa getting lost or screwing around with ads and games.

EPN Laptop Stand, Adjustable Laptop Riser with USB Cooling Fan, Ergonomic Computer Stand for Desk, Compatible with MacBook Pro Air, Dell, HP, Lenovo, More 9-16" Laptops, Aluminium Silver The EPN adjustable laptop stand is constructed of heavy-duty aluminum and feels sturdy. I tried it with both my 2017 15" Intel MB Pro and the redesigned 2020 16" MB Pro with a thicker bottom case.

I tend to lean my hands on the edge of my laptop, so I found the rise on the edge to be somewhat high when using it with my older computer, although I do appreciate having the extra fans for cooling on that model because Intel Mac Books Pro models tend to overheat.

This stand can handle the weight of both machines, with the latter coming in at over 4lbs, along with the weight of my hands leaning on it, and there was no indication of it wanting to sag or sink in any way. It will stay put at whatever angle or height you choose. At least it did for me.

I like having a slight angle when I type, and being able to raise my screen's camera to eye level so I am not looking down at it during Zoom meetings for that double chin effect. It's also convenient to have that little nook of space to tuck any cables and SSDs underneath, and out of the way.

There is about an inch to two inches of overhang on either side with larger computers, but it's not much, and both computers felt stable.

Overall, I would say it's a very good, and high-quality laptop stand. However, it is a bit smaller than I expected.
text_fidelity_b: EPN Laptop Stand, Adjustable Laptop Riser with USB Cooling Fan, Ergonomic Computer Stand for Desk, Compatible with MacBook Pro Air, Dell, HP, Lenovo, More 9-16" Laptops, Aluminium Silver

text_fidelity_a:
Nikon D3100 DSLR Camera with 18-55mm f/3.5-5.6 Auto Focus-S Nikkor Zoom Lens (Discontinued by Manufacturer) First, let me preface that I in NO way count myself a photog. I am just a shutter bug who has been firing frames almost non-stop since the age of 18. I learned on my dad's 'old' Nikon SLR with an f/1.2 lens. The Nikon SLRs/DSLRs I have owned are: N50, N60, N55, N80 and D50. My N50 ad N80 had the best lenses. The N60 and N55 were not as great and the D50 was a fabulous entry-level digital. The only medium format camera I own is my Holga. But hey, unlike the photographer at Portrait Innovations, at least I know 'medium format' does not refer to the number of megapixels at which I am shooting. As for my working knowledge, I had three semesters of photography in college. I can process/print both B&W and color film. (Not that that does me any good these days LOL) I can shoot completely 'manual' and I have stood among many pro photographers on the bridge at sunset, waiting for the color to be just right on Half Dome. (My Bogen tripod was way too heavy to be practical for an amateur but it gave me street credit.) So, in a nut shell, I shoot by the 'Sunny 16' rule. I know that opening my f-stop should increase my shutter speed give me a shorter depth of field; and, per the great Ansel Adams, f/8 is a proper exposure for all pictures.

That said, I hate my D3100.

I have had metering issues since I opened the box. I bought the camera so I could take 'even better' pictures of my infant son than I was getting from my D50. Ha. Joke was on me.

The contrast was BLINDING on the factory settings and every shot was over exposed. I have tried every metering option in the menu but the only changes I can achieve are under-exposure, blurred focus and missed shots. It's go high or go without.

I always lower my ISO to 100 when I'm outside because I crave rich color but it's just not there. I have tried Aperture Priority, Shutter Priority and Manual. Nothing. f/16 over my film speed on a sunny day. That's supposed to work! I have used it on many a 'less complicated' camera and achieved photos that make jaws drop. Well, there's no jaw dropping with this camera.

The metering overrides my manual choices every time. It's like I'm having a battle of wits with my camera. :( It reminds me of the days when Kodak was marketing 800-speed film as a universal, never-miss-a-shot solution to all your photo woes. Bleh. Just because there's always an image doesn't mean it's the RIGHT exposure.

I get that being an entry-level/made-for-the-masses DSLR really does mean it's a glorified point-and-shoot but it should preform at least as well as it's predecessors. Honestly, I got far more reliable results from my Canon SureShot and a roll of Kodak 100.

My expectation for a camera is that the image should be very close to perfect when the shutter closes. I know there's always room for improvement before printing but that's the art of photography. The hours I spend working on my photos after the shot should be to make them pop. Instead, my time is spent trying to rescue precious memories.

If you are considering this camera as your first DSLR because you think it will improve your skills, skip it. Invest in an equally expensive point-and-shoot that will give you all the same manual controls and preform much better in low-light situations. The D3100 does not live up to the standards of a Nikon SLR.

I gave it a second star because my son pulled mine off the counter about a year after I bought it and although the case cracked, it didn't seem to hurt the camera. Unfortunately, it impact didn't help it, either. (Yes, I was actually hopeful.)
text_fidelity_b: Nikon D3100 DSLR Camera with 18-55mm f/3.5-5.6 Auto Focus-S Nikkor Zoom Lens (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
SOSUN Video Camera Camcorder HD 1080P 24.0MP 3.0 Inch LCD 270 Degrees Rotatable Screen 16X Digital Zoom Camera Recorder and 2 Batteries(301S-Plus), 301AM I haven't bothered with a video camera in many years - using an excellent cell phone camera is just so much easier and convienent. That is still the case when I decide between using this camera vs my LG V40 phone for quick video of the dogs and horses. However, I did take the video camera with me to Big Bend National Park last week and tried it out there.

There are two rechargeable batteries and they offer far more use time than I expected. Swapping them out is pretty simple once you figure out where they go. The instructions are skimpy, but things are reasonably logical. The little carrying case is padded and the entire camera and case fits perfectly in a side pocket of a small hiking pack.

Actual use is straightforward. The camera fits in your palm and the record, photo and zoom buttons are designed to be pressed with just a thumb. I do like the view screen - it rotates and lets you really see what you're filming. For wide, expansive vistas like West Texas offers, this camera is fine and captures the vast distance of the landscape. However, close up details are fuzzy - I sincerely doubt this is true 1080p quality simply because the video shot from my phone is sharper and prettier. This is essentially a fine, basic little video camera that won't break a budget if it's lost or stolen.
text_fidelity_b: SOSUN Video Camera Camcorder HD 1080P 24.0MP 3.0 Inch LCD 270 Degrees Rotatable Screen 16X Digital Zoom Camera Recorder and 2 Batteries(301S-Plus), 301AM

text_fidelity_a:
Cyber Acoustics Stereo USB Headset (AC-5008A), in-line Controls for Volume & Mic Mute, Adjustable Mic Boom for PC & Mac, Perfect for Classroom or Home This headset does cancel noise, and the sound is clear. That part is fine. For the not-so-fine parts: they're really tight, and they cancel noise almost too well.

The tightness:
Right away, I felt that they squeezed my ears too much. I left them to stretch across several hard-bound books for a few days which loosened them up for a while, but they eventually go back to their original tightness that I can't wear them for more than 15 minutes at a time. My ears get squashed and they hurt to leave on, and I don't even have a big melon head!

The noise-cancelling:
While they do block out outside noise, they cancel my own voice out too, and I feel like I'm talking into a blanket by myself - I can barely hear myself talk. It's very disconcerting.

All in all, if they weren't so darn tight, I think I'd like them better. I had to dock 1.5 stars because of the physical discomfort, and .5 star for the talking-into-an-echoless-void factor. The sound quality is good, though. So, if you have a smallish head, and you like having all the outside sound shut out, they may work for you.
text_fidelity_b: Cyber Acoustics Stereo USB Headset (AC-5008A), in-line Controls for Volume & Mic Mute, Adjustable Mic Boom for PC & Mac, Perfect for Classroom or Home

Seagate FreeAgent Go 320 GB USB 2.0 Portable External Hard Drive ST903203FAA2E1-RK (Black) I bought a new laptop and didn't want to slow it down by downloading a bunch of software of music or videos. So, I purchased this product. When it arrived I plugged it in and transferred all of my iTunes music and videos immediately. I also put Rosetta Stone onto it. There was a constant humming sound but I didn't think much of it - assumed it was just working. I left it plugged in and put the computer on the table. I came back about a week later and tried to access my song files. No go. The computer would no longer even acknowledge that the Seagate FreeAgent was attached. I shut it all down, unplugged the Seagate, waited and then restarted everything...No go. I put the Seagate on a second computer - nothing. I tried a third computer - Nothing. I no longer have access to any of my files. All iTunes downloades are permanently locked away and cannot be accessed. Luckily Rosetta Stone had CDs but as for any other files, they're gone forever.
I tried Seagate and was told to retry what I had already tried which obviously did not work. Basically I paid for a black brick. I would not put any money towards this product or company again. I can't even begin to replace all that was lost.

Headphone Adapter Converter Supports Audio and Charging for Motorola MotoZ, Letv ,2 in 1 USB-C to 3.5mm Audio Adapter, Nylon Braided 2 in 1 USB Type C Cable Fast Charge to 3.5mm Audio Jack(Black) This is a much easier alternative to the My K-cup option if you want to use your own coffee in a K-cup machine rather than the pre-packaged cups. Unlike the My K-cup you don't need to remove the inner cup of the machine to use this. It just drops right in, so you can switch between this and a regular k-cup without having to dismantle anything.

The kit is very complete. There are three cups, each a slightly different color (different shades of brown). The cups are decently made. The plastic sides are nice and thick; the o-ring on the cap is of good quality; and the metal mesh is firmly attached. My only quibble with the build quality is the hinge. It's plastic, and I don't have confidence that it will last a long time before breaking. It's not a big deal, since the cup will still work fine even with a broken hinge, so I'm not docking any points due to that potential problem.

I like that the water dispersion channel has slots all around it to ensure water gets sprayed in all directions inside the cup to keep the grounds uniformly wet. I also really like that the lip area has a slight indent to make it very easy to pop open the top with one hand.

It fit fine in my Cuisinart K-cup machine. The lid of the machine was just slightly raised compared with using a "real" k-cup, but it had zero impact on performance. I tried several different brews, all with good results. You will need to fiddle with the grind level to get the best coffee. Too fine of a grind and it gets over-extracted and bitter; too coarse and it's weak.

Cleaning a used cup is very easy. I pop open the top, hold it upside down in the compost pail, and whack it gently on the base with a wooden spoon. Nearly all the used grounds drop out, and what's left can be easily rinsed under running water. You can also just dump the contents into the disposal or garbage if you don't compost your grounds.

Another option is to use a mini filter in the cup. A package of them are included and, while they do make cleanup easier, I prefer to use just the cup without a filter.

The kit also includes a charcoal filter. I didn't use that, so I can't speak to its performance. It looks to be the same size as the filters used in the water intake of my Cuisinart K-cup machine, so I expect it would perform in a similar fashion.

This Smart Cup kit works well, is well-made/designed, and comes in a very complete kit. Having used the My K-cup version I can confidently say that this performs better and is easier to use. Highly recommend.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Headphone Adapter Converter Supports Audio and Charging for Motorola MotoZ, Letv ,2 in 1 USB-C to 3.5mm Audio Adapter, Nylon Braided 2 in 1 USB Type C Cable Fast Charge to 3.5mm Audio Jack(Black)
